items.item: `Sources/Linux Kernel File Standard/Linux.Kernel.File.Clone.swift`: no test pins that `
items.reason: Copy.Range.copy takes a failure mapper so Clone.CopyRange maps the errno captured at the failing call (no reread). Capability.probe goes through internal Capability(kind:) on File.System.Kind. Tests (new Linux.Kernel.File.Clone Tests.swift): reflink only for btrfs/xfs; FICLONE on tmpfs (/dev/shm) returns false; copy range stops quietly at end of source; EBADF reported as .platform(.posix(EBADF), .copyFileRange). The cross-device FICLONE case is not tested (needs two filesystems).

items.item: `Sources/Linux Kernel IO Uring Standard/Linux.Kernel.IO.Uring.swift`: `next` never che
items.reason: `next` property became `mutating func next() -> Slot?` (nil when full); close(_:) throws Close.Error. Tests: next nil once full, drain stops at limit, enter interrupted by SIGUSR1 throws .interrupted (glibc only).

cpu is CPU.Logical.ID (non-negative by type), idle is new Thread.Idle(milliseconds: UInt32); Params.cValue throws .setup(.posix(EINVAL)) for a cpu above UInt32.max instead of trapping. Test target gains the CPU product.

all(_:) reads the named range from each image's runtime MetadataSections record (swift_enumerateAllMetadataSections via @_silgen_name), gated on the record version. Field layout checked with a standalone swiftc program on this machine (Swift 6.4.2, record version 5): index 14 is swift5_tests (one @Test gives 32 bytes). Tests in Linux.Loader.Section Tests.swift; test target now depends on Linux Loader Standard.
